findings.text: Once a queued voice mastermind starts, the bridge still thinks it is queued, and keeps thinking so until Servex restarts. `queued_why()` (RemoteMCP.js, diff line 127) reads `this.standins` before `agents.live`. The gate's stand-in (`Servex/Servex.js:1304`, `hold()`) always returns `state: "queued"` from `card()`, so the entry never clears. Every later ask on that connection says "waiting to start", and with a fallback set it is routed to the fallback forever. The fix is simpler too: drop `standins` and ask the gate itself, `this.servex.agents.queued_entry?.(id)` (`Servex/Servex.js:1185`). That also covers a queue restored after a restart, which the in-memory Map misses.

A `to` or fallback agent that is busy with other work has its words taken as the voice answer. `heard_event()` (diff lines 290–301) hands every delta of an agent to its oldest open ticket. When the turn ends without a reply file, `deliver()` makes those words the answer. So asking a working `vscode-mastermind`, or any running mastermind, can return the tail of an unrelated turn. The same race hits the voice mastermind if a new ask arrives while the last ask's turn is still running after its file was read. One fix: open the ticket's stream only after the `agent_msg` that carries this qid. Another: use turn-words as the answer only when the ticket's own message started that turn.

findings.text: The default fallback, `vscode-mastermind`, never streams, so it can lose an answer. The new message says "If your first sentence was the whole answer, skip the file" (`Servex/ext/remote/RemoteMCP.js`, diff line 180). But a VS Code tab is an external agent: `Agents.send` hands it to `external.deliver()` (`Servex/agents/Agents.js:613`), and no `delta`/`result` event ever reaches `heard_event`. A tab that follows the message and skips the file leaves its ticket at status "asked" forever, and nothing ever goes to the inbox. Fix: tell agents that are not in `agents.live` to always write the file, or say in the docs that say-first streaming works only for Servex SDK agents.

Test case 9 hides that gap. It fakes `vscode-mastermind` as a live streaming agent (`RemoteMCP.test.mjs`, diff line 418, then `live.set("vscode-mastermind", …)`), so "the fallback answers" passes for an agent shape the real fallback never has. Add one case with an external target that answers only through the reply file.

`.claude/skills/voice-mastermind/SKILL.md:14` still says "write the reply FIRST", meaning the reply file, before anything slow. The new "Say first" bullet just below says to stream one sentence before any tool call, and lets that sentence replace the file. Both point the same way, but line 14 should be reworded to match (the first review's note 8 is half done).

The loop in `heard_event` meant to answer "several queued asks" with one turn (diff line 302) only ever delivers `t`. Only the oldest ticket collects `words`, so `x.words` is empty for every other ticket. That is harmless, but the comment promises more than the code does.

findings.text: A follow-up asked while the mastermind is still on the previous voice ask loses its answer. Ask B arrives while ask A's turn runs, so B is unarmed (`busy`, RemoteMCP.js diff line 183). B only arms when B is the oldest open ticket and a `result` arrives (`heard_event`, diff line 305). A's own result is handled for A, and the loop at diff line 312 skips the unarmed B. So B's own turn only arms it, its words are dropped, and if the mastermind followed "skip the file" (it was told it streams), B never gets an answer. The next unrelated turn's words then become B's answer. This is the bridge's main case: a slow ask returns "Not answered yet", the owner keeps talking and asks again. Fix: on any `result`, arm every open ticket that was unarmed when that turn started, not only `open[0]`. Add a test with two voice asks in a row to the same streaming agent, the second asked mid-turn.

An agent with more than one turn queued ahead of the ask arms after the first of them (`armed` is one turn deep). A minion's "done" message queued behind the running turn would then have its words taken as the answer. `Agent.queued` (Servex/agents/Agents.js:2203) could set how many results to skip.

findings.text: `ahead()` counts the turns waiting in front of a new ask as `queue.items.length` (Servex/ext/remote/RemoteMCP.js:419). But the SDK reads `queue.stream()` as soon as a message is pushed, so a message that arrives while the agent is working sits in the CLI, not in `items`. The CLI's own count is `queued_turn_count` (Servex/agents/Agents.js:2202). So when the voice mastermind is mid-turn and a minion's "done" message is already waiting, an ask gets `ahead = 1` when the true count is 2. When the minion's turn ends, `deliver()` falls back to that turn's words because the reply file isn't written yet (RemoteMCP.js:351), and the owner hears the minion report as the answer. The fix: count turns with `a.queue?.kinds?.length`, which gets one entry per pushed turn and drops one at each result (Agents.js:1781); check how compaction turns affect it. Then add a test whose fake agent keeps `items` empty while messages wait. Test case 12 can't catch this today, because its fake agent has no queue at all.

When an ask's turn count is wrong (finding 1, or a `priority: "now"` message that jumps the queue), the comment at RemoteMCP.js:417 says the answer still arrives by its reply file. But a streaming agent is told "If your first sentence was the whole answer, skip the file" (RemoteMCP.js:327), so there may be no file to fall back on. After fixing 1, reword that comment, or always ask for the file.
